propositions: Compaction must work in stores without CI and without local cron, triggered from the close path out-of-band without holding the store lock across any operation a session waits on.

The scheduled sweep (6h cadence in CI) and the operation-linked trigger (detached worker spawned on close) together provide compaction coverage for both environments, but the sweep's per-ticket git history walk under the store lock causes multi-minute lock holds at scale, stalling concurrent writers.

Selection for recurrence must reuse the fold's own foldable-event predicate (events older than the horizon) to avoid selecting tickets whose excess is entirely young, which would be folded nothing and re-selected forever.
Honest reporting requires observing SNAPSHOT artifacts before and after the fold rather than trusting the return code, which reports 0 for both successful folds and all no-op branches.

The operation-linked trigger must not reintroduce the original P0 (13m53s lock hold on close) by running the fold inline; it spawns a detached worker that races neither foreground writers nor other compactors via a stamped advisory lock.
